item.title: Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg
item.description:
Databricks introduces Tag Exchange to share Unity Catalog tags via Iceberg

Databricks announced support for catalog labels, a new capability in the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API that enables platforms, engines, and agents to access context such as business purpose, ownership, and data classifications maintained in Iceberg REST-compatible catalogs. This development addresses the issue of metadata context remaining siloed in source catalogs, which previously forced teams to recreate classifications across platforms or maintain custom metadata synchronization pipelines.

🧩 How it works

Databricks worked with the Apache Iceberg community to add an optional labels field to the Iceberg REST LoadTable response. This provides a standard way for catalogs to expose table- and column-level context to other platforms, tools, and agents.

  • Labels format: String key-value pairs that describe business ownership, intended use, sensitivity, or other catalog-maintained context.
  • Flexibility: The standard defines a common format for sharing metadata without prescribing vocabulary or interpretation, allowing each platform to build on it in its own way.
  • Example: A table named support_cases can carry labels like domain=customer_support or system.certification_status=certified. An authorized data steward can also assign column-level labels, such as content_type=support_case_summary for an issue_summary column.

⚙️ Key details

Tag Exchange is Databricks’ implementation of this standard, exposing Unity Catalog’s table- and column-level tags through the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog API. This makes catalog metadata available directly to Python applications, including data-discovery tools and agents.

  • Open Governance: Context maintained in one system becomes usable across every platform, engine, and AI agent working with the data.
  • Reusability: Enterprises can reuse classifications and business context for discovery, agent workflows, and access policies.
  • Interoperability: Each tool retains the freedom to decide how to interpret and use that context, while the catalog’s metadata remains intact across platforms.

Databricks is joined by Google Cloud, Salesforce, ClickHouse, Atlan, Collibra, DataHub, Immuta, Trust3 AI, PhoenixAI, and Datastrato in advancing this shared vision of metadata interoperability.

🚀 Availability

Tag Exchange is available in Beta today. To get started, users can enable “Tag Exchange via Iceberg REST Catalog” in the Databricks Previews portal.

💡 Why it matters

This capability allows sensitivity labels set once in Unity Catalog to drive policy in external platforms without separate metadata projects. As noted by Don Bosco Durai, CTO of Trust3 AI, a sensitivity label set once in Unity Catalog can now drive policy in platforms like Trust3 AI without a separate metadata project. Similarly, Chandru Sugunan, Director of Product at Atlan, noted that open metadata exchange through the Iceberg REST Catalog lets enterprises keep context intact across every platform they choose to run.

#Databricks #ApacheIceberg #Metadata #TagExchange #DataGovernance #Interoperability

Source: Sharing catalog metadata across data platforms, engines, and agents

item.title: AWS Quick User Group DC Meetup Highlights FIG Analytics Platform
item.description:
AWS Quick User Group DC Meetup Highlights FIG Analytics Platform

On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, data leaders, developers, and practitioners gathered at the AWS Skills Center in Arlington, Virginia, for the AWS Quick User Group DC meetup. The session brought together founders, software engineers, and enterprise leaders, including a team from Financial Independence Group (FIG), to explore AWS Quick and participate in a hands-on application-building exercise.

🔍 Overview

  • Event: AWS Quick User Group DC meetup
  • Date: October 7, 2026
  • Location: AWS Skills Center, Arlington, Virginia
  • Attendees: Data leaders, developers, practitioners, founders, software engineers, enterprise leaders, and FIG team
  • Speaker: Vanessa Gonzalez, Vice President of AI at Financial Independence Group (FIG)

🧩 How it works

AWS Quick capabilities demonstrated at the meetup:

  • Agents and skills: Turn natural-language questions into multi-step reusable actions that aid in decision making across enterprise data
  • Built-in integrations: Connect tools like Salesforce, Slack, Google Drive, and Microsoft 365, breaking down data silos
  • Unified workspace: A cohesive environment that bridges research, automated visual generation, and business artifact creation (presentations, documents, and spreadsheets) directly where users work

⚙️ Key details

FIG’s implementation of AWS Quick:

  • Role: AWS Quick serves as FIG’s “single front door” for enterprise analytics
  • Data scope: Brings together structured data (CRM systems, databases, finance data) and unstructured content (internal knowledge bases, policy documents, collateral) through a governed data layer
  • AI analytics loop: Moves from reporting on what already happened to a continuous cycle: Ask → Analyze → Automate → Act
  • Centralized discovery: Analytics portal organized by business area (sales, operations, marketing, commissions) with built-in AI chat assistants so teams can talk directly to their documents and datasets
  • Democratized insights: Self-service exploration tools for non-technical business users, plus a learning hub that builds prompt engineering and AI skills across teams while keeping proper governance in place

🚀 Availability

Hands-on results from the meetup:

  • Every attendee successfully designed and launched a custom application in AWS Quick within 50 minutes
  • A subset of six participants built multi-step, event-triggered flows that handle repetitive data tasks
  • These flows replace manual reporting handoffs with automated, repeatable pipelines
  • New ideas now take hours or even minutes to build, not weeks or months

💡 Why it matters

  • FIG moved from existing analytics to AWS Quick to bring AI into its dashboards, reporting, and analytics
  • The platform enables a governed transition from static reporting to an continuous AI-driven analytics loop
  • Self-service tooling with embedded learning reduces time-to-insight for non-technical users while maintaining governance
  • Rapid application development (50 minutes for a custom app) accelerates organizational experimentation and deployment

#AWS #AIAnalytics #EnterpriseData #DataGovernance #WorkflowAutomation #BusinessIntelligence

Source: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Databricks and Google Cloud Announce General Availability of Bi-directional Catalog Federation
item.description:
Databricks and Google Cloud Announce General Availability of Bi-directional Catalog Federation

Today, Databricks and Google Cloud announced a significant milestone in catalog interoperability. Customers can now access a single copy of data from both Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s borderless Lakehouse through Lakehouse Federation, which is now generally available.

🧩 How it works

The partnership supports bi-directional interoperability, allowing data to move seamlessly between the two platforms without copying.

  • From Google Cloud to Databricks: Customers can mount Iceberg tables managed by Google Cloud’s Lakehouse runtime catalog into Unity Catalog. These tables can then be queried by Databricks Lakehouse (the serverless data warehouse) or analyzed via Genie, which answers data questions from natural language without requiring code or SQL.
  • From Databricks to Google Cloud: Data from Databricks can be brought into Google Cloud’s Lakehouse. This allows customers using engines like BigQuery to read Unity Catalog managed tables without data copy.

⚙️ Key details

Databricks and Google Cloud are strengthening interoperability by making catalog metadata open. They helped drive the landing of catalog labels in the Iceberg community, a proposal that enables catalogs to share metadata through key-value pairs.

Feature Description
Catalog Labels Enables catalogs to share metadata through key-value pairs (e.g., domain=finance, status=certified).
Tag Persistence Ensures table and column tags (e.g., pii=ssn) continue to be tagged even as the table is federated from one catalog to another.
Agent Context Shared labels provide context to agents searching for assets to answer data questions.
Data Masking Catalog metadata can be used to flag sensitive data for masking.

💡 Why it matters

Shared labels are critical for governance in the era of agents. By maintaining metadata consistency across federated catalogs, the partnership advances the vision of open governance, allowing sensitive data to be flagged and masked while providing necessary context for AI agents interacting with data assets.

Customers can get started with Catalog Federation between Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s borderless Lakehouse by reading the documentation.

#Databricks #GoogleCloud #DataInterop #UnityCatalog #Iceberg #DataGovernance

Source: Advancing Catalog Interoperability with Unity Catalog and Google Cloud’s Borderless Lakehouse

item.title: SAP and Infosys Argue Enterprise AI Needs Unified Data and Governance
item.description:
SAP and Infosys Argue Enterprise AI Needs Unified Data and Governance

SAP and Infosys executives are advocating for a shift in how enterprises approach AI, moving away from isolated pilots toward a unified platform model that integrates data, governance, and business processes.

🧩 From Pilots to Enterprise Platform

For years, organizations have treated AI as a series of discrete experiments. However, as AI agents begin to move into workflows that run the business, that model is becoming inadequate. The core challenge now is rethinking how data, business processes, governance, and people fit together to turn AI into part of the enterprise operating model.

Thorsten Leiduck, SVP and global head of SAP Business AI Platform Ecosystem, notes that many customers struggle to convert interest in AI into an operationalized model because programs often start as isolated proof-of-concepts (POCs) on inconsistent and fragmented data foundations. This fragmentation leads to duplication, inconsistent performance, and no clear path to scale.

⚙️ Key Components of the Shift

  • Unified Data Layer: Leiduck argues that AI is absolutely dependent on the data foundation. Companies need a connected, semantically rich layer that reflects their business before they can reliably deploy AI across processes.
  • Governance and Oversight: Clear policies, access controls, monitoring, and oversight are necessary to ensure agents remain trustworthy and aligned with business requirements. Leiduck and Singh agree that the absence of governance does not speed up adoption but instead creates a “risk backlog” that can force disruptive stops and audits.
  • Evaluation Framework: Satinder Pal Singh, associate VP North America for SAP BAIP and SAP AI Strategy at Infosys, recommends evaluating AI use cases through three lenses: impact, feasibility, and scalability. Companies must identify where an agent can move meaningful business metrics, ensure their data and talent can support the use case, and establish whether successful applications can be replicated.

💡 Why It Matters

As AI moves into mission-critical workflows, the stakes change significantly. Leiduck points out that while “80% might be good enough” for everyday applications, that level of accuracy is a “very terrible result” in areas such as supply chains or financial close. The goal is to move beyond AI as a mere productivity tool to “AI as a decision-making partner” that helps leaders understand what is happening, anticipate what comes next, and determine how to respond. Customer-specific knowledge graphs and governed data are becoming critical enterprise assets in this future.

#EnterpriseAI #AIAgents #SAP #Infosys #DataGovernance

Source: Building AI that can work across the enterprise

item.title: Analytics agents boost actionable insights to 48% but half remain ineffective
item.description:
Analytics agents boost actionable insights to 48% but half remain ineffective

Generative AI has broadened enterprise analytics, and the next wave—agentic AI—aims to automate whole workflows and act on the insights they generate.

🔍 Overview

  • Analytics agents are software assistants that surface descriptive and prescriptive insights for business users.
  • While most respondents praise the quality of descriptive insights, reviews of prescriptive insights are mixed.
  • Failure to produce business‑improving insights harms ROI, and flawed insights can cause reputational or financial damage.

📈 Performance Update

  • 48% of insights generated by analytics agents now lead to actions that improve the business. This is up from 37% a year ago.
  • More than half of the insights still do not help the business.
  • A small cohort called insight leaders achieves >70% actionable‑improvement rate and rates the quality of their agents’ insights higher than the overall respondents, especially for prescriptive insights.

⚠️ Challenges

  • The top reason agents produce substandard insights is a lack of business context (cited by 55% of executives).
  • Fragmented or inaccessible data is the second major factor (45%).
  • 52% of surveyed organizations say agents generate too many insights to be properly evaluated and acted upon.
  • Only 24% can evaluate all agent insights; most evaluations are done case‑by‑case and are human‑intensive.

🛠️ Improvement Initiatives

  • AI and data governance initiatives are a priority for 60% of companies to improve insight quality.
  • Adding a semantic layer to the data architecture is being pursued by 45% of respondents; experts interviewed stress that a semantic layer is crucial for high‑performing agents.
  • Insight leaders report fewer struggles with accessing business context.

🚀 Outlook

  • Agentic AI promises to move beyond delivering insights to automating entire workflows and taking actions based on those insights.
  • Closing the gap in context and data accessibility, and managing insight volume, are critical steps for more organizations to join the insight‑leader group.

#AIAnalytics #AgenticAI #EnterpriseAI #DataGovernance

Source: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics

item.title: New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors
item.description:
New Evaluation Semantics Profile for Croissant ML Dataset Descriptors

A new additive profile has been developed to provide evaluation semantics for Croissant, the de facto machine-readable descriptor for ML datasets.

🔍 Overview

While Croissant version 1.1 carries data use conditions—recommending ODRL and DUO—it does not specify how these are evaluated. It lacks a decision procedure, bounds on evaluation cost, outcomes for conditions an implementation cannot evaluate, records of what was checked, and information on composition with caller-side authority.

🧩 How it works

An additive profile allows a dataset to declare admitted operations and the conditions for those admissions. Key technical features include:

  • Closed Operator Set: Uses a closed set of five operators with a full decision procedure.
  • Automated Gating: A gate can decide based on the descriptor alone and record the checks performed.
  • State Space Separation: Caller-bound and data-bound policies range over non-overlapping state spaces, meaning neither permit set contains the other.

⚙️ Key details

Testing was conducted using two corpora with evidence kept apart, as well as a corpus generated from the profile’s grammar to cover every conformance clause, refusal class, and operator.

Deployment Results (nf-core pipeline)

Metric Result
Decision Accuracy Profile document decisions match the gate’s native descriptor record for record
Compatibility Stripping the layer leaves a valid Croissant document
Performance Cost 11.7 $\mu$s added cost against a 119 $\mu$s decision

Additionally, across valid cases, 552 complete decision records showed agreement between the native descriptor, profile terms, and the ODRL policy in usageInfo.

#Croissant #MLdatasets #DataGovernance #ODRL

Source: A Policy Profile for Croissant: Refusal as a Property of the Dataset

item.title: SPICE Up Your Analytics: Master QuickSight Dataset Management in One Dashboard
item.description:
🔍 SPICE Up Your Analytics: Master QuickSight Dataset Management in One Dashboard

𝙎𝙪𝙢𝙢𝙖𝙧𝙮: Struggling with Amazon QuickSight dataset management across multiple regions? This post introduces a comprehensive solution that combines AWS Glue, S3, and Athena to create an automated dashboard that gives you complete visibility into SPICE usage, dataset health, refresh status, and user permissions—all in one place. Say goodbye to manual monitoring and hello to optimized BI performance.

🧭 The QuickSight Management Challenge

Managing Amazon QuickSight across your organization brings a common yet frustrating challenge: how do you efficiently monitor dozens (or hundreds) of datasets spread across multiple regions and accounts?

If you’re like most QuickSight administrators, you’re constantly asking:

  • Is our SPICE refresh running successfully?
  • How much capacity are we consuming?
  • Which dashboards use which datasets?
  • Who has access to what?

The traditional approach—manually clicking through each dataset—quickly becomes unsustainable as your QuickSight environment grows. What if there was a better way?

🔧 Enter the Dataset Insights Solution

The solution we’re exploring automates the collection and visualization of critical QuickSight metadata, giving you a comprehensive dashboard that puts all your dataset insights in one place.

🏗️ How It Works

The architecture consists of three primary components working in harmony:

  1. Data Collection: AWS Glue jobs automatically extract critical information from your QuickSight environment using API calls and CloudWatch metrics.

  2. Data Storage: All extracted metadata is centralized in a dedicated S3 bucket, creating a single source of truth.

  3. Data Visualization: A purpose-built QuickSight dashboard displays actionable insights through Athena-powered queries.

📸 See illustration above showing the comprehensive solution architecture

🧩 What Gets Deployed

When you deploy the solution using the provided CloudFormation templates, you’ll get:

  • Six specialized AWS Glue jobs that extract different aspects of your QuickSight environment
  • A scheduled trigger to automate daily data collection
  • S3 storage for all your QuickSight metadata
  • Pre-configured datasets and data sources in QuickSight
  • A ready-to-use “SPICE Analytics Dashboard” with two information-rich sheets

🌟 Key Benefits and Insights

What makes this solution truly valuable is the comprehensive visibility it provides into your QuickSight environment:

𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗘 𝗨𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Monitor your SPICE capacity utilization with precision. The dashboard displays current consumption levels and allows you to set up alerts when you approach capacity limits—no more surprises when datasets fail to refresh!

𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗵 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝘂𝘀 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴

See at a glance which datasets are refreshing successfully and which have failed. No more hunting through individual dataset logs to find problems.

𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀

Understand the dependencies between your datasets, dashboards, and analyses. This is invaluable when planning changes or troubleshooting issues.

𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

Get full visibility into who can access what, making security reviews much simpler.

🚀 Getting Started in Four Simple Steps

Implementing this solution is straightforward with the provided CloudFormation templates:

1️⃣ Deploy the Data Collection Infrastructure

Use the first CloudFormation template to create the AWS Glue jobs, IAM roles, and S3 bucket needed for data collection.

1

Launch Stack: spice-usage-glue-jobs-stack

2️⃣ Run the AWS Glue ETL Jobs

After deployment, manually run each AWS Glue job once to collect initial data.

3️⃣ Configure S3 Permissions in QuickSight

Make sure QuickSight has appropriate access to the S3 bucket and Athena.

4️⃣ Deploy QuickSight Assets

Use the second CloudFormation template to create the dashboard, datasets, and data sources in QuickSight.

1

Launch Stack: spice-usage-QS-assets-stack

📸 See screenshot above showing the CloudFormation parameter input screen

Within 12 hours, your dashboard will populate with comprehensive data about your QuickSight environment, giving you unprecedented visibility.

🔮 What This Means for Your BI Strategy

This solution transforms how you manage QuickSight across your organization. Instead of reactive troubleshooting and manual checks, you gain:

  • Proactive monitoring with configurable alerts before issues impact users
  • Data-driven capacity planning based on actual usage patterns
  • Enhanced security oversight through comprehensive access visibility
  • Operational efficiency by quickly identifying orphaned or duplicate resources

The most powerful aspect? Everything is automated. Once set up, the solution will continue to provide fresh insights daily with minimal maintenance required.

🤔 Final Thoughts

As organizations increasingly rely on business intelligence for critical decisions, the infrastructure supporting those insights becomes just as important as the insights themselves. This QuickSight monitoring solution addresses a significant gap in the BI administration workflow.

Whether you’re managing a handful of datasets or hundreds across multiple regions, having a single-pane-of-glass view into your QuickSight environment allows you to focus less on administration and more on driving business value through data.

How much time could your team save with automated QuickSight monitoring?
